touches.text: Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."
Weekly: what is too long or too host-bound to run daily, such as hollow re-runs of every proof and each box's own run of the proofs it can run.

Sleep is an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9). Since there is one Cairn in the swarm (5.5.3.8.1), Cairn always starts the sleep token, however many boxes there are. At its time Cairn runs its own sleep routine, then hands the sleep token over the bus to the next device, and so on round the rack in the rack's order (5.7.3.3).

What each device does in its sleep depends on the device: the librarian consolidates memory; the learning blocks do the same on their smaller memory sets; Recovery might run backups or SSD checks; some (eg the embeddings device) do nothing.

Processes the sleep cycle, if its device needs one: when the token arrives, it wakes its device to do its sleep (the device does the sleeping, not the shim), then passes the token on. If its device won't come up, the shim files the trouble and still passes the token on, so the rest of the rack sleeps.
The pulse triggers the check: each pulse, the shim checks its device's list against the clock. No match, the pulse is dropped; a match is a PROBE that kicks off that thing in the device (5.6.4.6).
Part of the base shim, so every device can schedule things with it (eg Recovery's weekly SSD check is on Recovery's own list).

Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch().
